harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent RADIUS authentication from node2 to node1 on CentOS 5.11. Valid credentials are accepted, invalid credentials rejected, and an incorrect client secret is not accepted. Both nodes passed sequential restart and recovery verification.
actions_performed: Configured a dedicated protected client secret for node2 and synchronized it securely.
Configured the demonstration user from access.txt without modifying the handover.
Enabled radiusd and a persistent node2-only UDP/1812 firewall rule on node1.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified recovery after each.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated node2 client and demonstration user configured
evidence.summary: The node2 client definition uses the protected server secret, the configured user matches access.txt, both nodes hold matching secret hashes, and radiusd is listening.
Post-restart testing recorded one Access-Accept for correct credentials, one Access-Reject for wrong credentials, and zero approvals plus an invalid-signature error for the wrong secret.
access.txt and client-notes.txt retain identical checksums before and after configuration and restarts.

evidence.requirement: Legacy operating-system release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5.
Captured healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered radiusd/listener/firewall/data, and successful authentication.
Captured healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, persistent secret/handover data, and successful post-restart authentication.
